title: bpTorch Sample Gallery
description: 25 trainable architecture demonstrations showcasing the diversity of visual blueprint programming.

samples.name: Arch 1: nanoGPT Tiny
samples.description: Canonical tiny GPT with hierarchical subgraphs: embeddings, blocks, attention, and LM head.
samples.highlight: Best starting point for exploring compositional transformer blueprints.

samples.name: Arch 2: nanoGPT Deep (6L)
samples.description: Six-layer transformer stack for studying depth scaling and gradient flow.
samples.highlight: Shows how repeat stacks compose deep models from reusable block subgraphs.

samples.name: Arch 3: nanoGPT Wide (1L/8H)
samples.description: Single-layer, eight-head wide transformer emphasizing parallel attention heads.
samples.highlight: Demonstrates width-vs-depth tradeoffs in a compact blueprint.

samples.name: Arch 4: Two-Layer MLP
samples.description: Classic two-layer perceptron with GELU activation for tabular/feature tasks.
samples.highlight: Simplest trainable blueprint — ideal for first edits and property tuning.

samples.name: Arch 5: Bottleneck Autoencoder
samples.description: Encoder-decoder MLP with a narrow bottleneck for representation learning.
samples.highlight: Illustrates hourglass topology and reconstruction-style training.

samples.name: Arch 6: Manual Attention Transformer
samples.description: nanoGPT variant wired with explicit manual causal attention instead of SDPA.
samples.highlight: Peel back the attention black box — every matmul is visible on the canvas.

samples.name: Arch 7: Dual-Flow Pipeline
samples.description: Event-driven training graph with separate data and execution flows.
samples.highlight: Blueprint training as a visual program: dataloader → forward → backward → optimizer.

samples.name: Arch 8: ResMLP Residual Network
samples.description: Residual MLP block with LayerNorm and skip connections.
samples.highlight: Residual wiring without transformers — shows skip connections in pure MLP form.

samples.name: Arch 9: Multi-Head Projection
samples.description: Explicit QKV split, head split/merge, and SDPA attention wiring.
samples.highlight: Every attention primitive is a separate node — maximum transparency.

samples.name: Arch 10: Multi-Task Network
samples.description: Shared backbone with parallel LM and classification heads plus weight tying.
samples.highlight: Fan-out topology with tied embeddings — one backbone, two objectives.

samples.name: Arch 11: ReLU Classifier MLP
samples.description: Two-layer MLP using ReLU instead of GELU for sharp activation boundaries.
samples.highlight: Swap activations in one property — compare ReLU vs GELU behavior.

samples.name: Arch 12: Dropout MLP
samples.description: Feedforward network with dropout between hidden layers.
samples.highlight: Regularization as a first-class blueprint node, not a hidden flag.

samples.name: Arch 13: Deep MLP Tower
samples.description: Five stacked linear+GELU layers without any attention.
samples.highlight: Pure depth — see how deep feedforward towers compose from primitives.

samples.name: Arch 14: Wide-and-Deep Network
samples.description: Parallel wide memorization path and deep generalization path fused with Add.
samples.highlight: Google-style wide-and-deep architecture built from basic nodes.

samples.name: Arch 15: Tied-Embedding LM
samples.description: Minimal language model: embedding → LM head with shared weights.
samples.highlight: Smallest possible LM — weight tying visible as an explicit binding.

samples.name: Arch 16: Warmup Scheduler Pipeline
samples.description: Dual-flow graph with linear warmup LR scheduler node.
samples.highlight: Learning-rate schedules as blueprint nodes in the training event graph.

samples.name: Arch 17: Step-LR Decay Pipeline
samples.description: Dual-flow graph with step-wise learning rate decay.
samples.highlight: Compare scheduler strategies side-by-side with Arch 16.

samples.name: Arch 18: Pre-LayerNorm MLP
samples.description: MLP with LayerNorm before each linear layer (pre-norm pattern).
samples.highlight: Normalization placement is a wiring choice, not framework magic.

samples.name: Arch 19: Residual Add MLP
samples.description: Single residual block using an explicit Add node for the skip connection.
samples.highlight: Skip connections drawn as visible edges — not buried in module code.

samples.name: Arch 20: Binary Sequence Classifier
samples.description: Token embedding → linear head for binary sequence classification.
samples.highlight: NLP classification without transformers — just embeddings and a head.

samples.name: Arch 21: High-Dropout Transformer
samples.description: nanoGPT with 20% dropout for regularization-heavy training.
samples.highlight: Tune dropout on the canvas and watch training dynamics change.

samples.name: Arch 22: BF16 nanoGPT Micro
samples.description: Tiny nanoGPT configured for bfloat16 mixed-precision training.
samples.highlight: Mixed precision is a training property — cook and run with --precision bf16.

samples.name: Arch 23: Single-Block Causal GPT
samples.description: Smallest causal transformer: one block, four heads.
samples.highlight: Minimal transformer for teaching attention without stack complexity.

samples.name: Arch 24: SiLU Deep Feedforward
samples.description: Two-layer MLP with SiLU (Swish) activation.
samples.highlight: Three activation primitives (GELU, ReLU, SiLU) — pick yours on the canvas.

samples.name: Arch 25: Metric Logger Pipeline
samples.description: Dual-flow training graph with a Metric Logger node in the exec chain.
samples.highlight: Observability wired into the training program — metrics as blueprint nodes.
